**Proposed mechanism:** MTTP (HGNC:11972) —DISRUPTS→ Chylomicron and VLDL assembly (REACT:R-HSA-1937206); APOB (HGNC:709) —DISRUPTS→ Chylomicron and VLDL assembly (REACT:R-HSA-1937206); Chylomicron and VLDL assembly (REACT:R-HSA-1937206) —LEADS_TO→ Abetalipoproteinemia (MONDO:0008692); APOA1 (HGNC:704) —PRODUCES→ Amyloid fibril (CHEBI:50740); Amyloid fibril (CHEBI:50740) —LEADS_TO→ Amyloidosis, hereditary systemic 3 (MONDO:0971008). Loss-of-function mutations in MTTP or APOB impair the assembly of chylomicrons and VLDL, leading to abetalipoproteinemia. Gain-of-function mutations in APOA1 lead to the production of amyloidogenic APOA1 variants that form amyloid fibrils, causing hereditary systemic amyloidosis 3. The convergence is on APOA1, which is critical for lipid transport in abetalipoproteinemia and can itself become pathogenic in amyloidosis.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of mutations in APOA1 that are clearly loss-of-function in nature and associated with abetalipoproteinemia, or conversely, identification of mutations in MTTP or APOB that are clearly gain-of-function and associated with amyloidosis. _(variant: gnomAD v2.1.1 shows no variants in APOA1 with allele frequency > 0.001 that are strongly predicted to be pathogenic and linked to amyloidosis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the dual role of APOA1 in lipid metabolism and amyloid formation could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting both lipid disorders and amyloidosis. For instance, therapies aimed at stabilizing APOA1 or enhancing its clearance could be beneficial in amyloidosis, while therapies to improve lipid transport could indirectly affect amyloid deposition.

#### 9. Alzheimer disease 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.333)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8963888)

**Proposed mechanism:** MTTP (HGNC:11978) —DISRUPTS→ Apolipoprotein B secretion (GO:0003012); Apolipoprotein B secretion (GO:0003012) —LEADS_TO→ Abetalipoproteinemia (MONDO:0008692); APOE (HGNC:716) —DISRUPTS→ Lipoprotein metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-180906); Lipoprotein metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-180906) —LEADS_TO→ Alzheimer disease 2 (MONDO:0007089). Mutations in MTTP disrupt the secretion of Apolipoprotein B, leading to abetalipoproteinemia. In contrast, certain APOE variants (associated with Alzheimer disease 2) disrupt normal lipoprotein metabolism, contributing to neurodegenerative processes.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in MTTP that confers a gain-of-function phenotype or a pathogenic variant in APOE that confers a loss-of-function phenotype, in the context of these specific diseases, would falsify the proposed mechanistic link.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of lipoprotein metabolism and APOE in both abetalipoproteinemia and Alzheimer disease 2 could reveal novel therapeutic targets for modulating lipid handling in neurodegenerative disorders or improving lipid absorption in genetic lipid transport defects.
